name: Priya

income.note: Effective tax rate ~25.5% including federal + TX (no state income tax)

savings_breakdown.note: 401K started at 24, 6% contribution with 3% employer match. HYSA is emergency fund (covers ~3 months expenses). Below Fidelity 1x salary benchmark of $95K by age 30 — a source of anxiety.

debt_breakdown.student_loan_note: Private university CS degree. National avg for engineering-related tech bachelor's is $41,308. Priya's lower balance reflects partial family contribution.
debt_breakdown.credit_card_note: Slightly below Millennial avg of $6,961 (Experian 2025). Carries balance most months at 21.5% APR — pays above minimum but doesn't fully clear.

financial_goals: Pay off credit card debt within 18 months
Reach 1x salary in retirement savings by 30
Save for home down payment by 32-33
subscription_note: Typical of Millennials who carry 6-11 active subscriptions (industry research, 2024). Two subscriptions are unused in the last 60 days.

behavioral_profile.money_script: I should be doing better financially given how much I earn — but somehow there's never enough left over.
spending_triggers: Stress at work (buys something small as reward)
Seeing peers post purchases on Instagram/LinkedIn
Feeling burned out — self-care purchases spike
cognitive_biases_observed: Lifestyle creep: expenses have grown proportionally with every raise
Mental accounting: treats credit card rewards as 'free money'
Present bias: delays paying off credit card to enjoy monthly surplus
Social proof: buys trending items she sees on social media
shopping_patterns: Primarily shops on Amazon and Instagram Shop
74% of Millennials impulse buy regularly (GoDaddy 2024 — Priya fits this)
Researches for 1-3 days before purchases over $100
Uses Amazon wishlists as a 'cooling off' mechanism (sometimes)
behavioral_profile.financial_anxiety_notes: 52.3% of Millennials rate financial stress impact on mood at 7+/10 (PlanAdviser). Priya experiences 'money dysmorphia' — feels financially behind despite earning above median. 58% of Millennials experience financial anxiety 3+ days/week.
behavioral_profile.homeownership_note: 58% of Millennials feel forced to choose between homeownership and retirement (Nationwide 2025). Priya is in this cohort.

demo_context.coaching_note: Priya can technically afford this from surplus but it conflicts with her credit card payoff goal. Present bias and self-reward framing are likely active.
